findings.problem: Lines 51–89 repeat the two-scale construction in exists_two_normalized_annular_returns: derive nonzero finite mass from strict smallness and local finiteness, select returns at both radii, and transport their bounds through multiplication by κ. The substantive difference is the additional property enforced at each selected return. Maintaining these constructions separately risks inconsistent changes to the mass requirements or annular bounds.
findings.proposed_change:
Introduce a shared exists_two_normalized_annular_returns_ae lemma with exactly the parameters and hypotheses of exists_two_normalized_annular_returns, followed by `(P : ℝ → Prop) (hP : ∀ᵐ u ∂intrinsicRootLeaf hij μ x, P u)`. Its conclusion should be:
`∃ t : Fin 2 → ℝ, (∀ b, P (t b) ∧ rightAction x (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.transvection hij (t b)) ∈ K ∧ rightAction y (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.transvection hij (t b)) ∈ K) ∧ ρ ≤ |κ * t 0| ∧ |κ * t 0| ≤ 1 ∧ 16 / ρ ≤ |κ * t 1| ∧ |κ * t 1| ≤ C`.
Proof sketch: retain the shared radius, positivity, nonzero-mass, finite-mass, choice, and normalization arguments; replace the single-annulus call by exists_annular_simultaneous_root_return_ae with P and hP, and carry the chosen P proofs into the conclusion. This consolidates the complete construction, rather than just extracting its short arithmetic calculation. Place the helper in TwoAnnularReturns.lean, importing LeafReturnCovariance there, and import TwoAnnularReturns in the target; the inspected dependency chain permits this without a cycle.
Both rewritten uses, under their existing hypotheses, have the following form:
```
-- exists_two_normalized_annular_returns
obtain ⟨t, ht, h0l, h0u, h1l, h1u⟩ :=
  exists_two_normalized_annular_returns_ae hij μ K G c a hgood
    x y hx hy heq hloc κ ρ C hκ hC hsecond hsmall hcoeff
    (fun _ => True) (by filter_upwards [] with u; trivial)
exact ⟨t, fun b => ⟨(ht b).2.1, (ht b).2.2⟩,
  h0l, h0u, h1l, h1u⟩

-- exists_two_normalized_annular_equal_leaf_returns
rw [← heq] at hrebasey
let P : ℝ → Prop := fun u =>
  intrinsicRootLeaf hij μ
    (rightAction x (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.transvection hij u)) =
  intrinsicRootLeaf hij μ
    (rightAction y (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.transvection hij u))
have hP : ∀ᵐ u ∂intrinsicRootLeaf hij μ x, P u := by
  filter_upwards [hrebasex, hrebasey] with u hx hy
  exact hx.trans hy.symm
obtain ⟨t, ht, h0l, h0u, h1l, h1u⟩ :=
  exists_two_normalized_annular_returns_ae hij μ K G c a hgood
    x y hx hy heq hloc κ ρ C hκ hC hsecond hsmall hcoeff P hP
exact ⟨t, fun b => ⟨(ht b).2.1, (ht b).2.2, (ht b).1⟩,
  h0l, h0u, h1l, h1u⟩
```
Keep all existing hypotheses unchanged: in particular, do not add positivity of ρ. Strict smallness already excludes zero outer mass, while local finiteness supplies finite outer mass.
findings.benefit: One shared two-scale selection proof governs both results, while each public theorem exposes only its distinguishing property. Readers no longer need to compare nearly identical constructions to understand why equal terminal leaves can also be enforced.
